dāṭhā.cp: fem. a fang; the canine tooth.
dāṭhā.p: [Daṃsa+ṭha+ā] (thī) CL=8 Dhāna,ṭī.261.ṇvādi.56. Ḍaṃsa+ṭha+ā. Dāṭhāti cadantaviseso. So hi ḍaṃsati etā-yāti dāṭhāti vuccati. Ḍaṃsaneti dhātu-to ṭha-paccayavasena ḍaṃsissa ca dā-kā-rādesavasena padasiddhi veditabbā. Jā,ṭī,1.149.(daṃ-saṃ, dāḍhā-prā, addhamāgadhī)]   (1) (a) (fangs of snakes, canine of dogs, etc.). (B) the eyetooth (of the Buddha) . See original. (2) it look like eyetooth/canine and it is sharpen as canine (four kind of Noble Magga, etc.,).  dāṭhī- see.
pn: Dāṭhā. Daughter of Aggabodhi I. She was given to the Malayarājā, the sister’s son of Aggabodhi I. (Cv.xlii.6, 10), who afterwards became Aggabodhi II. (Cv.xlii.64). She seems to have been also called Saṅghabhaddā. (Cv.xlii.41).

[ BHS dāṭhin; cf S. daṃṣṭrin], having large teeth or fangs; having tusks ; Ja II 29, 17* (~ini; 29, 21´ : bhadde dāṭhāsampanne sīhi); 245, 23* (so hi tattha mahā hoti sigālo viya ~inaṃ; 246, 3´ : yathā sigālo ~īnaṃ mahā ahosi evaṃ mahā hoti); 409, 14* (vyagghaṃ migā yattha jiniṃsu ~ino; 409, 19´ : ~ino sūkarā migā); IV 348, 14* (~ī ~īsu pakkhandi; 348, 16´ : sayaṃ dāṭhāvudho itaresu dāṭhāvudhesu pakkhandi); V 302, 21* (soṇā vakā sigālā ca ye c’ aññe santi ~ino); Th p 1, 3* (sīhānaṃ va nadantānaṃ ~īnaṃ girigabbhare; Th-a I 6, 25 : ~īnan ti dāṭhāvantānaṃ); Th 524 (deve gaḷantamhi nadanti ~ino; Th-a II 220, 18 foll. : ~ino ti sīhavyagghādayo paṭipakkha-sattā, te hi dāṭhāvudhā ~ino ti vuccanti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee tehi dāṭhāhi vuyhantī ti ~ino ti).

pn: Dāṭhika. A Damiḷa usurper. He slew Piḷayamāra and reigned at Anurādhapura for two years, till he was slain by Vaṭṭagāmaṇī Abhaya. Mhv.xxxiii.59, 60, 78; Dpv.xix.15, 16; xx.17, 18.

--āvudha [Sk．daṁṣṭrāyudha] using a tusk as his weapon J.V，172； --danta a canine tooth KhA 44； --balin one whose strength lies in his teeth （of a lion） Sn.72．（Page 318）

（၁） （က） （မြွေ，ခွေး-စသော သတ္တဝါတို့၏） အစွယ်။ （ခ） （ဘုရားရှင်၏） စွယ်တော်။ မူရင်းကြည့်ပါ။ （၂） အစွယ်နှင့်တူသော၊ အစွယ်ကဲ့သို့-စူးရှ-ထက်မြက်သော （အရိယမဂ်လေးပါးစသည်）။ ဒါဌီ-ကြည့်။

V: Dāthā：Daughter of Aggabodhi I．She was given to the Malayarājā， the sister&#39；s son of Aggabodhi I．（Cv.xlii.6，10），who afterwards became Aggabodhi II （Cv.xlii.64）．She seems to have been also called Sanghabhaddā． （Cv.xlii.41）.

( and dāṭha, m. ) [ cf S. daṃṣṭra, daṃṣṭrā, and S. lex. dāḍhā, BHS -dāṭha], 1. a canine tooth; a fang ; Abh 261; D II 167, 26* (ekā pi ~ā tidivehi pūjitā); Bv 28:6 (ekā ~ā tidasapure); Ja I 273, 17 (so yakkho … kandamakulamattā dve ~ā ca māpetvā); II 27, 7 (sīho … ekaṃ mahisaṃ vadhitvā ~āhi ovijjhitvā); IV 181, 23 (catūhi ~āhi, Be, Ce so; Ee ~ehi; Se dāḍhehi); V 231, 25 (sunakho … mukhaṃ vivaritvā catasso ~ā dassetvā); VI 166, 15´ (nāgamāṇavā … ~ā vivaritvā passasantā aṭṭhaṃsu); Sv 450, 16 (kāci ~ā kāḷā pi vivaṇṇā pi honti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr dāthā); 604, 10 (catasso ~ā dve akkhakā uṇhīsan ti imā satta dhātuyo na vippakiriṃsu); Dhp-a I 215, 8 (agadena kira ~ā dhovitvā ekaṃ sappaṃ pesetū ti); — 2. a tusk ; Ja II 408, 5 (sūkaro … vyagghaṃ … ~āya paharitvā); Mhv 25:29 (~āhi bhinditvāna silā … hatthī); — °’ āvudha , mfn. , whose weapon is his teeth or fangs ; Ja IV 348, 16´ (sayaṃ ~o itaresu ~esu pakkhandi); V 172, 15* ; Nidd I 8, 4 (sappo … dāṭhā tassa āvudho ti ~o, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se dāḍhā … dāḍhāvudho) = Sadd 466, 25 ; Cp 2:10:1 (~o ghoraviso dvijivho uragādhibhū, Be, Ce so; Ee wr daṭhāvudho; Se dāḍhāvuso; Cp-a 175, 12 : catasso dāṭhā āvudhā etassā ti ~o); — °- danta , m.
